name: Bariatric AI
tagline: AI assistant for bariatric surgery patients: meal logging, protein and fluid targets, and stage-aware post-op food guidance.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip away the branding and this is a food log with a protein-and-fluid dashboard plus a chat model carrying a post-op stage in its system prompt. An agent will get you that in an afternoon, and the math is trivial: grams of protein, ounces of fluid, days since surgery, a stage gate on what textures are allowed. The parts that are not trivial are the ones you use on a phone at a restaurant: barcode scanning, a decent food database, and a log you actually open three times a day. Food data is solvable with USDA FoodData Central, which is free, but it is still a third-party dependency and it is thin on restaurant items. Also worth saying plainly: your build will give the same generic LLM advice this category tends to give, just without the reassuring logo.
coreLoopDIY: Logs meals against USDA nutrition data, tracks daily protein and fluid against targets, and answers questions with a chat model primed on your surgery date and current post-op stage.
requirements: A free USDA FoodData Central API key
Node 20 and somewhere to run it, a laptop or a cheap VPS
Your surgery date and whatever targets your actual care team gave you
whatYouLose: A real mobile app with barcode scanning, which is the whole point of logging at the moment you eat
A curated bariatric food database with brand items and portion presets instead of raw USDA entries
Content that has been reviewed by someone with a dietitian credential, which matters more here than in most app categories
Any clinic-side features: sharing progress with a surgeon or program, HIPAA-shaped handling of your data
Nudges, reminders and streaks, the boring retention machinery that is why anyone sticks with a tracker
moatNotes: Health guidance sells on who appears to be standing behind it. A self-hosted prompt with no clinician anywhere near it is a different product even when the output text is identical.
whyPeopleStillPay: Post-op patients are tired, nauseous, and following a stage schedule they half remember from a pre-op class. They want one app that already knows what week four allows, that scans a yogurt cup, and that feels like it came from the medical side of the fence rather than from a weekend project. Paying a few dollars a month to not think about any of that is a rational trade, and the alternative is a spreadsheet they abandon in nine days.
notes: The build is easy; the discipline to log every meal in a web app you wrote yourself is not.
prompt:
Build a local-first post-op nutrition tracker called "Protein Log" as a Next.js 15 App Router project with TypeScript and Tailwind. Single user, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud.

Storage: SQLite via better-sqlite3 at ./data/app.db, created and migrated on first boot. Tables: profile (surgery_date, procedure_type, protein_target_g, fluid_target_oz), entries (timestamp, food_label, grams, protein_g, calories, carbs_g, fat_g, fluid_oz, note), foods_cache (fdc_id, label, per_100g macros, fetched_at).

Secrets in .env.local only: OPENAI_API_KEY, USDA_FDC_API_KEY. Never commit them, ship .env.example.

Screens:
1. Today: big protein and fluid rings against targets, a chronological list of today's entries, inline delete and edit.
2. Add entry: a search box hitting USDA FoodData Central, results list, pick one, enter grams or a preset portion, app computes macros and writes the row. Cache every food hit in foods_cache so repeat searches work offline. Allow a manual free-text entry with hand-typed protein and fluid for restaurant food.
3. Ask: a chat panel calling the LLM with a system prompt that includes procedure_type, days since surgery, the computed current stage (clear liquids, full liquids, pureed, soft, regular, derived from a stage table in a single editable config file), today's protein and fluid totals, and an explicit instruction to refuse dosing, medication and complication questions and to tell the user to contact their surgical team instead. Render a persistent banner on this screen: not medical advice, follow your program's plan.
4. History: last 30 days as a table plus a protein-per-day sparkline, and a "Export CSV" button.

In scope: the four screens, the stage config file, CSV export, a seed script with three sample days.
Out of scope: barcode scanning, auth, multi-user, push notifications, native apps, any sync.

Keep it to one sitting of code: no component library beyond Tailwind, no state manager, server actions for writes. Write a README that says how to get both API keys, how to set the profile row, and that the stage table is a placeholder the user must replace with the one their own program gave them.
